accuracy.evidence: Z = protons, A = protons + neutrons, ions from electron loss/gain, shells 2,8,8,2 for Z ≤ 20; all challenge targets (Li-7, F-19, Mg2+, Cl-, Ca2+, O2-, Al-27, K+) checked against standard isotope data.

misconceptions.evidence: Predictions target 'electrons or mass decide the element' and 'electrons have no charge'; challenge catches neutrons = A, swapped A/Z and the wrong sign of ion charge.

lab_distinct.evidence: Particle-by-particle atom builder with a live nuclear-symbol card; specific to counting protons, neutrons and electrons.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner sees the name change only when protons change, the mass number change with neutrons, and the charge appear when electrons are removed.

predictions.evidence: Step 1 tempting wrong answers 'electrons' and 'how heavy'; step 2 'a different element'; step 4 '-1' — each is disproved by the build.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six distinct messages: swapped numbers, wrong protons, neutrons = mass number, wrong neutrons, reversed charge direction, neutral atom electrons.

readability.evidence: Validator readability limits pass; kid text uses short sentences and one idea per paragraph.

no_filler.evidence: No filler phrases; every paragraph carries a rule or a worked example (carbon-14, sodium-23, Na+, Cl-).

mobile.evidence: iPhone 13 screenshots: symbol card fits after the width fix, bins and +/- buttons reachable, nothing clipped.

accessibility.evidence: +/- buttons for every particle as an alternative to drag; canvas aria-label describes the atom live; axe clean in both themes.

sources: IUPAC Gold Book: mass number, atomic number
Royal Society of Chemistry periodic table data
